messages:
ida: Running AWQ-FP8 bakeoff on A800 cluster (CUDA14 / TensorRT-LLM) — hitting a hard failure and weird quality delta. start ->

ida: command i used:
```
rcli run --model redwood/transformer-xl --quant awq-fp8 --backend tensorrt-llm --cuda 14 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --profile perf,accuracy
```

sam: can you paste the logs / error?

ida: paste from node (trimmed):
```
[TRT-LLM] kernel compile failed: unsupported dtype mapping for fp8-e5m2 -> kernel fallback to host
[TRT-LLM] attention_cuda.cu:assert(threadIdx.x < blockDim.x) failed
[Runtime] falling back to CPU attention for layers [10-12]
```

ida: also see a bunch of `CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED` lines right after.

devops-bot: heads-up — GPU driver was rolled forward to 535.54 on these nodes 2 days ago as part of infra upgrade.

maria: interesting. we haven't validated FP8 path on CUDA14 + TRT-LLM yet. most of our QA used CUDA12/13 + Triton or vLLM.

rahul: quick eval numbers from the failing run (same prompt set):
- baseline fp16 (vLLM/CUDA13): 78.6% accuracy
- AWQ-FP8 (TensorRT-LLM/CUDA14): 74.2% accuracy (-4.4)
- GPTQ-INT8 (vLLM/CUDA13): 77.9% (-0.7)

rahul: also perf: FP16 throughput 120 tok/s, AWQ-FP8 on TRT-LLM dropped to 30 tok/s (lots of CPU fallback).

sam: that looks like a dtype/kernel mapping issue in TRT-LLM for the AWQ fp8 layout, causing partial CPU fallback which both kills perf and may change numerics. can you repro with triton backend?

ida: i reran with backend=triton and cuda=13 on same model and quant config:
- AWQ-FP8 (Triton/CUDA13): accuracy 78.1% (within noise), throughput 140 tok/s

ida: so the problem is specific to TensorRT-LLM + CUDA14 stack.

maria: do we have a repro snippet that isolates the attention path? if TRT is compiling a kernel that thinks fp8 layout is e4m3 vs e5m2 that could silently alter values.

ida: minimal repro attached below (trimmed) — running locally with same docker image used by CI:
```
# docker run -v /models:/models redwood/inference:staging-2026-03 
python -m redwood.runner --model /models/transformer-xl --quant awq-fp8 --backend tensorrt-llm --cuda 14 --check-attention
```

logs show dtype mapping `fp8_e4m3` -> `fp8_host_mapped` at compile time.

sam: can you check tensorrt-llm version? we recently shipped 0.4.2 which had a mapping change; 0.4.3 is staged with a potential fix.

ida: tensorrt-llm==0.4.2 on the cluster. 0.4.3 not rolled to these nodes.

deploy-bot: rolled tensorrt-llm 0.4.3 image to staging (group=ml-candidate) at 1764810000.

ida: i'll re-run the same job on staging nodes with 0.4.3 + CUDA14 and post numbers.

rahul: suggested acceptance criteria for onboarding: reject quantized model if delta > 1.0% vs fp16 on our eval suite, unless flagged for retrain/tuning. we should add driver/backend matrix to the gating checks.

maria: agreed — add a matrix entry: (model, quant, backend, cuda_version) -> eval delta. if backend causes CPU fallback we should fail fast.

sam: meanwhile, workaround: pin nodes to CUDA13 + Triton or vLLM for AWQ-FP8 workloads until TRT-LLM 0.4.3 validation completes. add a runtime routing rule: backend_prefers: triton for quant=awq-fp8.

ida: quick update after re-run on staging (tensorrt-llm 0.4.3, cuda14):
- AWQ-FP8 (TRT-LLM/0.4.3/CUDA14): accuracy 78.0% (good!), throughput 110 tok/s (some degradation vs Triton but no CPU fallback), logs show fixed dtype mapping.

ida: i'll open a PR to add (CUDA,backend) matrix checks in model-onboarding and add a note in the README about known combos to avoid until validated.

maria: please also add an eval threshold check to the onboarding pipeline and a step that interrogates runtime logs for "falling back to CPU" as an immediate fail case.

ida: will do. re-run full bakeoff across A800 cluster tomorrow and post detailed numbers + traces.

sam: thanks — super helpful. tagging infra to consider fleet rollback if any production jobs run on those CUDA14 nodes with TRT-LLM 0.4.2. :thumbsup:
